The indicator measures the number of structured and purposeful knowledge exchange activities implemented as part of a project. These activities are designed to facilitate the sharing of information, expertise, and experiences among different stakeholders on the importance of protecting groundwater.

description.narrative: The indicator measures the number of trainings for officials at different administrative levels conducted on ground water governance and management. Potential topics of the training include: Groundwater governance, Conjunctive surface, Groundwater management and Protection, water and gender for the promotion of gender equality and women empowerment, and on the collection of gender disaggregated data using the UNESCO WWAP Toolkit.

title.narrative: Up to 5 pilots illustrating appropriate Innovative techniques for sustainable conjunctive use of groundwater and surface water resources. "

description.narrative:
The pilots shall include the following: a) Managed Aquifer Recharge (MAR) interventions: the MAR will be piloted in two sub-basins of the Nile. At least one pilot will be integrated with improving water supply for a small – medium sized town dependent on groundwater.
Pilot Water Funds for sustainable watershed services to improve groundwater recharge and upstream downstream collaboration will be explored. c) Use of advanced remote sensing for monitoring and management of shared groundwater aquifers. d) Use of isotope hydrology technique for detailed modelling of interaction between ground and surface water for specific (selected) wetland ecosystems. Under this pilot, a detailed model for surface water – groundwater interaction will be developed and linked to the NB DSS.

title.narrative: Number of countries (shared aquifers) with SADA report completed

description.narrative:
This indicator measures the number of countries with shared aquifers that have completed SADA (Shared Aquifer Diagnostic Assessment) reports
The SADA report include geological and hydrogeological maps, new conceptual models, and new information on connection between surface waters and groundwaters within the Nile based Region covering 3 shared aquifers namely the Kagera transboundary aquifer, Mt Elgon Aquifer and Gedaref-Adigrat sandstone transboundary aquifer
An aquifer is an underground layer of rock or sediment that contains water and releases it in appreciable amounts.
This indicator measures the number of harmonized ground water action Plan developed covering: information on water depth, ground water flow and recharge and management systems.

title.narrative: Harmonized and standardized groundwater knowledgebase (geodatabase and maps) for all the three shared aquifers in place with all pertinent information.

description.narrative:
This indicator measures the number of knowledgebases developed for the 3 shared aquifers namely the Kagera transboundary aquifer, Mt Elgon Aquifer and Gedaref-Adigrat sandstone transboundary aquifer
The knowledgebase will comprise aquifer maps and geo-database of key aquifer attributes. The aquifer maps shall, at a minimum, include aquifer areal extents, water table elevation, key water recharge areas, key water demand centers they support (if any), and water quality status (using key parameters) with identified water quality hotspots.

title.narrative: Technical manual and guideline to support conjunctive use of SW and GW (the manual/guideline will address measures to enhance MAR and sustainable yields, measures for water quality protection, conservation of groundwater dependent ecosystems, institutional mechanism to promote conjunctive use of SW and GW, and sustainable of groundwater dependent ecosystems)

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of technical manuals and guides designed to support conjunctive use groundwater and surface water resources. These technical manuals and guides will address, among others, measures for enhancing aquifer recharge (such as through MAR- Managed Aquifer Recharge) and sustainable yield, water quality protection, and conservation of groundwater dependent aquatic ecosystems linked to the selected aquifers.

description.narrative: This indicator quantifies the number of strategy documents that have been successfully scaled up from their initial pilot project and integrated into the broader framework of national-level IWRM activities. It measures the extent to which strategies developed for specific pilot initiatives have influenced and become part of the national water resources management framework.

title.narrative: Number of trainings for technicians, academics, and senior planners undertaken on key requisite techniques on groundwater monitoring and sustainable management with gender issues given high priority

description.narrative: "The indicator measures the number of trainings for technicians, academicians and senior planners conducted on ground water monitoring. The subjects of the trainings will include: - Gender mainstreaming in Groundwater Management; water and gender for the promotion of gender equality and women empowerment, the collection of gender disaggregated data using the UNESCO WWAP Toolkit - Groundwater assessment using ground based and remote sensing data sources - Hydrogeology and groundwater recharge estimation - Groundwater modelling - Aquifer mapping - Planning and Implementing Managed Aquifer Recharge - Groundwater governance - Conjunctive surface and groundwater management and protection"

title.narrative: Regional Shared Aquifer Integrated Management Action Plan (collection of recommended measures addressing gaps and threats identified in Component 1 developed and Submitted to Member states

description.narrative:
"This indicator measures the number of shared Aquifer Integrated Management Action Plan developed covering:
a) Actions for improving groundwater monitoring using ground and remote sensing-based technologies. ie monitoring the status of the groundwater resource base (water levels, recharge, water quality) as well as its use (abstraction). b) Technical manuals and guides support conjunctive use groundwater and surface water resources. c) Recommended institutional mechanisms for sustainable management and utilization of the groundwater resource. Further, the recommendations will also cover aspects for strengthening national inter-sectoral coordination to promote protection and sustainable conjunctive use of surface and groundwater resources. Gender aspects will be integrated in all recommendations with the aim improving roles of women and youth in groundwater resources management. d) Measures for maintenance of groundwater to sustain groundwater-dependent aquatic ecosystems (wetlands, floodplains and river reaches). e) Strategies for conjunctive surface and groundwater use as a key climate change adaption measure at national and regional levels. "
